storedPurchase (purchases.ts:209-231) answers by token hash before any Play call. The repeat test for _15 asserts 200, an unchanged gets count, 15 credits and one row. It passed in CI.
purchases.ts:243 throws INVALID_INPUT before storedPurchase or any Play call. The application_pack_99 test asserts zero Play calls and zero rows.

There are two layers. (a) productId present: purchases.ts:187 rejects a mismatch. The c5 test stages productId application_pack_5 without boughtAs, so the fake skips the path check and the in-app equality check is the thing under test. It would fail if :187 were removed. (b) productId absent (L1, adjudicated): the path cannot be redirected after the allow-list. The request is parsed once (purchases.ts:330). pack is found by === on request.productId (:240-242). That same unmodified string goes to verifiedPurchase (:250-255) and then to play.getProduct (:163). play.ts:162 builds products/${encodeURIComponent(productId)}/tokens/..., and :167-168 maps 400/404 to PlayRejectedError, which purchases.ts:165-169 maps to PURCHASE_INVALID. settleConsume also uses the config productId stored in the row (:265, :102). Exploiting L1 needs all of the following: Play drops productId, Play also ignores the path product, and the token is the caller's own purchase (obfuscatedExternalAccountId binding, :194). So it cannot cross accounts. I accept the Fixer's disagreement with fail-closed and close L1 with no finding. The new path-bound test and the boughtAs fake model the binding faithfully for that token only. The fake is still permissive by default, which is deliberate: it keeps the c5 test exercising :187. The test proves the PlayRejectedError -> PURCHASE_INVALID mapping and that nothing is granted. It does not prove live Play behaviour. Residual risk: verify path binding on the internal test track as part of tailor-my-resume#288 before _15/_40 go live.
